I added `reverseResolveAlias(path: string, aliases: Record<string, string>): string[]` to `src/utils.ts`, right after `resolveAlias`. Its body is just `throw new Error("not implemented");` and its doc comment follows the style of the other functions in the file.

- **Existing code:** every existing export (`normalizeAliases`, `resolveAlias`, `filename`) and every internal is unchanged. `src/index.ts` doesn't re-export the new function, as the spec requires.
- **Types and constants:** the spec doesn't name any, so I added none. The function takes the same `Record<string, string>` alias map that `resolveAlias` uses.
- **Errors:** the doc comment says nothing about throwing, because the spec says the function never throws for string inputs. It does say that the function returns `[]` when nothing matches, and that results come back as a new array, sorted longest first.
- **Checks:** `npx tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit` reports no errors, and `npx vitest run` passes all 362 tests, the same as before. `src/utils.ts` is the only file I changed.

Added: `reverseResolveAlias`

public.finalText:
I gave the file the wrong extension: it used `.test.ts` when the instructions called for the `.spec.ts` ending the existing tests use. It's now `test/pathe-reverse-alias-confirmed.spec.ts`, and its contents are unchanged.

After the rename, `npx tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit` reports no errors. `npx vitest run test/pathe-reverse-alias-confirmed.` finds the file and runs it: 46 tests fail because the function body throws `not implemented`, which is expected. The 2 that pass are the `[happy-10]` checks that `resolveAlias` hasn't changed, since they don't call the new function. Nothing else in the repo was touched.

48 tests, in 1 file.
